questions.prompt: What values can a Pauli observable return in this lesson?

options.text: Only 0 and 1
+1 and -1
Any probability between 0 and 1
Only complex amplitudes

questions.explanation: Pauli X, Y and Z have eigenvalues +1 and -1, which are averaged to estimate an expectation.

questions.prompt: What is the Z expectation for 70 positive and 30 negative outcomes?
questions.explanation: The signed mean is (70-30)/100 = 0.40. The positive probability alone is 0.70.

questions.prompt: Which analyzer measures X using a standard Z detector?

options.text: No gate and then Z
H and then Z
X and then X
Measure the same collapsed state twice

questions.explanation: H maps the X eigenbasis to the computational basis before the Z detector.

questions.prompt: How is an expectation different from P(0) in the Z basis?

options.text: It is P(0)+P(1)
It is P(0)-P(1) for Z eigenvalues +1 and -1
It is always equal to P(0)
It cannot be estimated from counts

questions.explanation: The signed Z average assigns +1 to zero and -1 to one, so it is P(0)-P(1).

questions.prompt: For C=<Z>+0.5<X>, with estimates 0.40 and -0.20, what is C?
Why are fresh preparations usually needed for non-commuting terms?

options.text: A measurement collapses the state and changes the later experiment
Fresh shots make every probability exactly one
Non-commuting terms have no eigenvalues
The optimizer requires a new qubit name

questions.explanation: Different basis settings ask different questions, so using one collapsed batch would not estimate the intended observables.

questions.prompt: What does increasing the shot count usually improve?

options.text: Sampling uncertainty, but not a wrong circuit or systematic bias
Every source of hardware error
The exact Hamiltonian definition
The need for a basis change

questions.explanation: More shots narrow finite-sample variation. They do not repair modeling, readout or device bias.

questions.prompt: Which statement about a weighted cost is correct?

options.text: Every cost must be a probability
Weights can combine signed term expectations into an objective
All terms must be measured in Z
A single outcome is the exact expectation

questions.explanation: Costs and energies are often weighted sums of expectations, which may be negative or outside the probability range.

questions.prompt: What should be reported with a sampled expectation?

options.text: Only the largest histogram bar
The term, analyzer, shot count and estimate
Only the final optimizer angle
The statevector instead of the experiment

questions.explanation: Those details make the estimate reproducible and help distinguish shot noise, basis mistakes and implementation errors.
